newsitem.title: UK: British Gas unit plans to be large domestic player.
newsitem.headline: British Gas unit plans to be large domestic player.

text.p: British Gas Plc subsidiary British Gas Energy (BGE) plans to become one of the leading suppliers of electricity to domestic customers when the market opens to competition in 1998, the Sunday Times said.

"Power industry executives who have had contact with the company say BGE aims to enter the business at the first opportunity, with the target of eventually supplying 10 percent of the market's 22 milllion homes in England and Wales," the newspaper said.
BGE is the trading arm of British Gas, which will be demerged next year.

The paper said the move would boost the company's profits by enhancing economies of scale and in the supply business. With 19 million customers at present, GGE's residential business is almost as large as the domestic electricity market, it said.

"Subject to approval by Offer and Ofgas, the industry regulators, it will be perfectly positioned to offer customers a single bill for both gas and electricity," it added. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
